en: Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for its perfect cone shape and is the most active volcano in the Philippines.
The Philippine eagle is the national bird and is endemic to the remaining old-growth forests of the island of Mindanao.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley before emptying into the Babuyan Channel.
Lake Taal in Batangas is a freshwater volcanic lake located inside a large caldera formed by massive prehistoric eruptions.
Palawan is the longest province in the Philippines, stretching southwest between the South China Sea and the Sulu Sea.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of at least 1,268 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting diverse coral reefs.
The Benguet province in the Cordillera Administrative Region is a major producer of highland vegetables and contains rich gold deposits.
Mount Kitanglad Range Natural Park in Bukidnon is a protected area known for its mossy forests and rare wildlife.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The Tamaraw, a dwarf buffalo found only on the island of Mindoro, is a critically endangered endemic species of the Philippines.
